title: Sections of a set-valued constant etale sheaf on a connected scheme
statement: Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, let $U$ be a nonempty connected scheme [def-pc-scheme] over $\Omega$ [def-weil-connected-scheme], and let $E$ be a set. For the constant sheaf $\underline E$ on $U_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], the canonical map $E\to\underline E(U)$ is a bijection. It is natural under every $\Omega$-morphism $v:V\to U$: the pullback of the section corresponding to $e\in E$ is the constant section with value $e$ on $V$, with no connectedness hypothesis on $V$.

source.place: Remark 59.23.2 (Tag 03P5, label etale-cohomology-remark-constant-locally-constant-maps), the set-valued form: sections are Zariski-locally-constant maps and a locally constant map on a connected nonempty space is constant

proof.text: Let $U_E=\coprod_{e\in E}U$ and let $h_{U_E}$ be the representable presheaf on $U_{\Et}$. By [lem-galois-constant-sheaf-sets-representable], the constant sheaf $\underline E$ is canonically isomorphic to $h_{U_E}$, and the canonical constant section associated to $e$ corresponds to the morphism $\iota_e\circ\mathrm{id}_U:U\to U_E$. Thus $\underline E(U)$ is identified with the set of morphisms $U\to U_E$ over $U$.

Apply [lem-galois-coproduct-copies-morphisms-clopen] with $W=U$ and $s=\mathrm{id}_U$. A morphism $U\to U_E$ over $U$ is an $E$-indexed clopen decomposition of $U$, equivalently a map $|U|\to E$ with open fibres. By [lem-weil-pbc-connected-locally-constant-map], every such map is constant because $U$ is nonempty and connected. Therefore exactly one index $e$ has piece $U$ and all other pieces are empty, so every section is the unique constant section with value $e$; nonemptiness makes the value unique. Hence $E\to\underline E(U)$ is bijective.

source.place: Remark 03P5 (remark-constant-locally-constant-maps): locally constant maps on a connected nonempty space are constant

proof.text: Let $v:V\to U$ be an $\Omega$-morphism. By Step 1 the canonical map $E\to\underline E(U)$ is $e\mapsto\eta_U(e)$, the image of $e$ under the canonical map $\eta$ from the constant presheaf, and the section corresponding to $e$ is $\eta_U(e)$. Its pullback along $v$ is $v^*\eta_U(e)\in(v^{-1}\underline E_U)(V)$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] (with $U\times_UV=V$), and the canonical isomorphism $\gamma_v:v^{-1}\underline E_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\underline E_V$ of [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-constant-sheaf] sends it to $\eta_V(e)$, the constant section with value $e$ on $V$. Nothing about $V$ is used, so the naturality holds without any connectedness assumption on $V$.
